portal_hypertension.title: Cirrhosis, portal hypertension and hepatocellular carcinoma: a stage-based approach.
portal_hypertension.authors: Allaire M, Taddei T, Thabut D
portal_hypertension.zhSummary: 该文聚焦门静脉高压症，属于综述研究。核心观点：尽管有重叠，但目前的指南将门静脉高压症和肝癌分开处理，导致风险分层和治疗选择不理想。 临床提示：CSPH 与肝硬化失代偿风险增加相关，其...
portal_hypertension.abstract: Cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) are interconnected outcomes of chronic liver disease, with portal hypertension playing a key part in cirrhosis decompensation, and influencing HCC prognosis and treatment. Despite their overlap, current guidelines address portal hypertension and HCC separately, leading to suboptimal risk stratification and treatment selection. This Review proposes a stage-based, integrated approach to HCC management that incorporates the prognostic stages of cirrhosis and emphasizes clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH) as a key stratifying factor in compensated cirrhosis. portal_hypertension.title: Anticoagulation in Patients With Gastrointestinal Disease.
portal_hypertension.authors: Alkasabrah O, Ramesh J, Shah RK
portal_hypertension.zhSummary: 该文聚焦门静脉高压症，属于临床研究。核心观点：胃肠道 (GI) 疾病会同时增加出血风险并维持较高的血栓栓塞脆弱性，从而使抗凝治疗变得复杂。 临床提示：粘膜损伤、门静脉高压、恶性肿瘤、炎症性肠病和血管病变容易导致出血，而中断治疗会增加中风、静脉血栓栓塞和支架植入的风险
portal_hypertension.abstract: Gastrointestinal (GI) disease complicates anticoagulation by simultaneously increasing bleeding risk and maintaining high thromboembolic vulnerability. Mucosal injury, portal hypertension, malignancy, inflammatory bowel disease, and vascular lesions predispose to hemorrhage, whereas interruption of therapy increases the risk of stroke, venous thromboembolism, and stent thrombosis. Contemporary management follows an indication-first, risk-balanced approach that integrates thrombotic urgency, GI disease phenotype, and patient-specific bleeding-risk factors.
